title_en: The Sharia Sciences Series — Tape Two
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم نبدأ إذن بما بدأ الله به فنبدأ بكتاب الله سبحانه وتعالى، وكتاب الله يتعلق به كثير من العلوم الإسلامية، من أهمها : علم حفظه وأدائه ثم علم تفسيره ثم علوم القرآن ثم بعد ذلك علم القراءات ويضاف إليها علم الرسم والضبط، فلنبدأ بحفظ القرآن: لا شك أن الذي يُحَفظُ القرآن يحتاج إلى مهارات عديدة لذلك، وهذه المهارات التجربة الإسلامية فيها كفيلة بأن تجنب الإنسان كثيرا من الأخطاء التي وقع فيها كثير من محفظي القرآن السابقين، الذين يشرفون على حلقات تحفيظ القرآن أو يباشرون تدريس الصبيان وتحفيظهم لهم رصيد كبير من تجارب العالم الإسلامي في هذا الباب، وهذه التجارب كثير منها أصبح محل هزء وسخرية لدى الناس فقد ألف كثير من المؤلفين فيما يتعلق بطرائف محفظي القرآن والتنكيت عليهم، فيذكرون أن رجلا رأى في النوم أنه يمضغ الحصى فأتى ابن سيرين فسأله عن ذلك فقال تكون معلما للصبيان..
body_en: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. We begin, then, with what God began with, so we begin with the Book of God — glorified and exalted is He. Many of the Islamic sciences attach to the Book of God, the most important of them being: the science of memorising it and of rendering it aloud (adāʾ), then the science of its exegesis (tafsīr), then the Qur'anic sciences, then after that the science of the canonical readings (qirāʾāt), to which is added the science of its orthography and its vocalisation. So let us begin with the memorisation of the Qur'an. There is no doubt that one who has the Qur'an memorised needs numerous skills for that; and as for these skills, the Islamic experience in them is enough to spare a person many of the errors into which many of the earlier teachers of Qur'an memorisation fell. Those who supervise Qur'an memorisation circles, or who undertake the teaching of boys and the hearing of their memorisation, have a great fund of the Muslim world's experience in this matter; and many of these experiences have become an object of mockery and ridicule among people, for many authors have written on the amusing anecdotes of the Qur'an memorisation teachers and the jokes made at their expense. They relate that a man saw in his sleep that he was chewing pebbles, so he came to Ibn Sirin and asked him about it, and he said: you will be a teacher of boys..

flags.note: adāʾ here is the recitational sense — delivering the text aloud correctly — NOT the glossary's worship sense, 'performance in its proper time', which belongs to the law of making up missed acts. The glossary rendering must not be applied to this passage. Same class of error as applying the five rulings to a creedal proposition (style guide section 8): check what the term attaches to before using the fixed rendering.

translator_notes: A course lesson on how the Qur'anic sciences are ordered, and on the practice of teaching memorisation. No legal ruling is given; the passage on mockery of memorisation teachers is descriptive reportage of a literary genre, not a judgement upon those teachers.

'يُحَفظُ' is vocalised in the source as the passive of form II, which would mean 'is taught to memorise'; the sentence as a whole reads more naturally of the person who has memorised, and it is rendered that way. The vocalisation is the CMS's, not necessarily the Sheikh's.
